db/postgres#

PostgreSQL driver over the frontend/backend protocol 3.0, written in Okkama: framing (db/postgres/wire), SCRAM-SHA-256 and MD5 (db/postgres/auth) and the conversation below.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let database = PostgresDatabase(
    PostgresTcp(IpEndpoint(IpAddress("127.0.0.1"), 5432)),
    PostgresCredentials("app", SecretBytes(Utf8Encoded("secret").bytes())),
    PostgresOptions("app"),
    SystemEntropy());
let connection = await database.connection();
let rows = await connection.rows(Statement("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1", [DbInteger(7)]));

Description#

PostgreSQL driver over the frontend/backend protocol 3.0, written in Okkama: framing (db/postgres/wire), SCRAM-SHA-256 and MD5 (db/postgres/auth) and the conversation below. The host supplies only TCP, TLS and crypto.

Every statement goes through the extended query protocol, so parameters never become SQL text and one Statement is one SQL command. Placeholders are PostgreSQL's own $1..$n. Parameters are sent untyped (OID 0): the server infers each type from its context, and a context-free parameter needs an explicit cast ($1::int8). Text, integer, floating and decimal values travel as text literals, booleans as true/false, bytes in binary format.

Results come back in text format and decode by column type: bool as DbBoolean, int2/int4/int8/oid as DbInteger, float4/float8 as DbFloating, numeric as DbDecimal, bytea as DbBytes; NaN and infinities are a data failure, every other type (dates, json, uuid, arrays...) is DbText. Column.declaration() is the type name (int4, text...) or "oid:<n>".

A query is one round trip: Bind, Execute without a row limit and Sync go out together, and the server streams the whole answer through ReadyForQuery. The reader decodes it batch rows at a time as it is read from the socket, so TCP flow control bounds what is buffered. While a row reader is open the connection is busy; closing it early discards the rest of the answer on the next operation (the server has computed it anyway). Only one operation runs at a time per connection.

Authentication accepts trust and SCRAM-SHA-256 (no channel binding); MD5 and cleartext passwords are refused unless PostgresOptions enables them. SCRAM requires the server's final signature before AuthenticationOk. PostgresTls sends SSLRequest and verifies the server certificate; PostgresTcp is plaintext. Server diagnostics surface as DbFailure with the SQLSTATE as code and a driver-written message (server text may echo bindings).

object PgTransport#

object PgTransport does Closing

Byte transport of one connection: the startup conversation and everything after it run over input/output; close() ends the connection. A transport with a cancel route lets the session stop a long answer whose reader closed early (#240); without one, the rest of that answer is read through.

role PgCancelRoute#

object PostgresDatabase#

object PostgresDatabase

A PostgreSQL database to connect to.

PostgresDatabase.PostgresDatabase#

PostgresDatabase(transport is PostgresTransporting, credentials is PostgresCredentials, options is PostgresOptions, entropy is Entropy)

The database reached through transport, logging in with credentials; entropy makes SCRAM nonces.

PostgresDatabase.PostgresDatabase#

PostgresDatabase(url is string)

A server named by a URL (#218): PostgresDatabase("postgres://app:secret@db:5432/shop?sslmode=require"). The host is looked up by DNS. sslmode=disable, the default, talks plaintext; require, verify-ca and verify-full talk TLS checked against the system's trust store and the host name; prefer and allow are refused. The database is the user's name when the path is empty.

PostgresDatabase.PostgresDatabase#

PostgresDatabase(url is string, password is SecretBytes)

The password kept apart from the URL: PostgresDatabase(url: Environment().text("DATABASE_URL"), password: secret).

object PgSession#

object PgSession does Closing

One protocol conversation. Every operation holds the lock, first resolves work left by closed readers, statements and abandoned transactions, and reads the server's answer through ReadyForQuery before releasing it. An operation interrupted mid-conversation (cancellation, transport failure) closes the connection, since the protocol position is then unknown.

PgSession.portion#

async portion(operation is DbOperation, outcome is PgOutcome) is PgOutcome

The next batch rows of a streaming answer, or the rest of it up to its end; an ended answer is read through ReadyForQuery (its request carried Sync). Otherwise the rest stays on the wire for the next portion, or for settle to discard when the reader closes early.

PgSession.drain#

async drain(operation is DbOperation) is void

The rest of an answer whose reader closed early, discarded through ReadyForQuery. Its failures belong to nobody; fatal ones still close the connection. Past 8192 rows or 1 MiB of discarded rows, a transport with a cancel route asks the server to stop the statement (#240): the short remainder then ends with SQLSTATE 57014, which is dropped like any other failure here.

PgSession.observe#

observe(message is PgMessage, outcome is PgOutcome) is bool

Records one message; true when the server awaits COPY data, which the caller refuses with CopyFail.

PgSession.refuse_copy#

async refuse_copy(operation is DbOperation) is void

The server ignores a Sync that arrives in copy-in mode, and the request's own Sync already has; after CopyFail it waits for another.

PgSession.settle#

async settle(operation is DbOperation) is void

Deferred cleanup of closed readers, statements and abandoned transactions; runs under the lock before any new request. An open reader owns the rest of its answer, so nothing is settled until it closes.
